title: Professor Cobb's cornet lessons and early lodge drummers
summary: At seven he takes two weeks of lessons from Professor Cobb, who tells his mother he has no musical aptitude; he then notices lodge bands and drummers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: So how did you come to play at the theater?

Well, what happened was, when I was about seven, there was a man that played a cornet, named Professor Cobb, a rarity. And I asked my mother if I could take lessons with Professor Cobb, and she said yes. And Professor Cobb taught me for two weeks, 25 cents a lesson. And then he talked to my mother and he said, "Mrs. Price, your son ain't got it. He just don't have it. He don't understand what it's all about." And she said, "Well, do you think that he can learn?" He said, "He can never learn. He has no conception of music and no conception of rhythm and no conception of tonal qualities, so that's that. So just save your 25 cents." And this sort of, you know, cooled me down for a while. But when I was seven or eight, then you started having drummers, and lodges and various

organizations would have...then they started developing bands where that you had a bass drummer that played the bass. They didn't have all these contraptions...all this new stuff. The guy had a cymbal on the top of the bass and he played a mallet. He played the bass drum with a mallet. And then you had a man playing the snare drum. But you know what I'm thinking...perhaps these things were not accessible to black communities so this may be a reason why I wouldn't know, I would not be exposed to it. If it's in a white theater you just pass by and see, Tom Thumb or some band or something, but it would not mean anything to me because of the fact that I didn't ever have an opportunity to see it, you know, to get inside that theater and to really get close up to the drummer, because they didn't allow blacks in many of those places.
